findings.problem: The rework step 05 (H1) made an end of the question's range that is missing or not a valid integer 'no bound' while the other end still bounds, and the check calls the shared helper ctx.int with that end as null. ctx.int prints its second text 'Число N вне границ от a до b' with a = null when only the upper end is set. I ran it on the sketch with the real validator and the real check function: a number question with no min (or min = the string x) and max 1000, chips [-5, 1001] gives the line «questions[2].chips[1]: E_LIMIT: Число 1001 вне границ от null до 1000. Исправьте значение.»; the project's own line-shape helper (lineProblems) marks it 'parser' because the word null is on the list of words no message may hold (the same list as design F7 and the rule of 6.4). I ran 600 combinations of min, max and chips: 12 distinct such lines, all for a missing or non-integer min together with a chips item above max (a missing min is a common mistake in a tenant file); with a missing max (min set) the text is the existing «не меньше N» and is fine. No named test sees it: F22 and LK-5b assert code and place only, LK-7a reads the 78 samples (none has this case), LP-1 changes look, desk, chips, object, whatsapp, max_per_hour, max_stored and questions but never min or max of a question. No call of ctx.int in the released code has (min null, max set) and D15 lists only two changes of shared helpers, so this is a new use of a shared mechanism that nobody checked (AP-014). Before H1 the design said 'an invalid min skips the range' and the problem did not exist.
findings.needed: Make the line of that case obey the shape rule. Smallest change: return to 'the range of chips is checked only when BOTH ends of the question are valid integers; otherwise only the integer form of each item is checked' (D8, 5.6, F22 case 1, the first case of LK-5b, MU66 reworded accordingly); keep or add in LK-5b a case with a missing min and a chips item above max whose expected result is the lines of the question's own min error and no chips line, and let LP-1 (or LK-5b) check lineProblems on it. The other possible fix (keep H1) needs a new catalogue message for a one-sided bound, its sample row and a test; it is larger.

findings.item: A3 (named test must see the mutant)
findings.problem: SV-9b only checks that no string of B stands in A's answers and the reverse. A look cached in a module variable is seen by SV-9b only when the first look to fill the cache is that of A or B. If an earlier test of the same file fills it with a third look (SV-9d builds one), A and B both show the third look and SV-9b stays green; SV-9a (values equal the file) then catches it. In my first model of the tests MU52 was red in SV-9a and SV-9e and not in SV-9b for this reason.
findings.needed: Bind MU52 to SV-9a and SV-9b, or let SV-9b also assert that the answer of A holds A's own headline and staff name and the answer of B holds B's.
